title: The Canticle, whole (Francis)
hook: sun, moon, wind, water, fire, earth, and death, all praising
tomorrow: what comes first: doing something, or looking?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hildegard's viriditas: the green, fresh life of God in leaves, in fields and in souls. The line was greening.

Some families can't say the word death at the dinner table. Others plan the funeral songs over dessert. Most of us sit somewhere in between, changing the subject. Francis of Assisi wrote a song that names death out loud and calls her Sister: Sister Bodily Death, whom no living person can escape. And he says it kindly, as one more voice in a long praise of everything God made.
screen: `THE WORD NOBODY SAYS AT DINNER.` → `SISTER BODILY DEATH.` → `SAID KINDLY.`

segments.voice: It's the Canticle of the Creatures, in Francis's own Italian dialect, not in Latin. First, the opening. Most high, almighty, good Lord: praise, glory, honor and blessing belong to you. Then the refrain begins: Laudato si', mi' Signore, praised be you, my Lord. Second, the sky. Brother Sun, who brings the day and is radiant, carries your likeness, Francis says. Sister Moon and the stars, clear and precious and beautiful. Brother Wind, and air and cloud and every kind of weather. Third, the ground. Sister Water, useful, humble, precious and pure. Brother Fire, who lights the night, cheerful and strong. Sister our Mother Earth, who feeds and rules us, with her fruits and colored flowers and herbs. Fourth, the people and the end. Praise for those who forgive for love and bear trouble in peace. And then Sister Bodily Death. Tradition says Francis added those last verses later, the death verse near the end of his own life. He doesn't make death an enemy. He gives her a place in the family, and the song closes: praise and bless my Lord, give thanks, and serve him with great humility. For a family facing it this week, that's what the song offers: a way to say the word without running.
screen: `LAUDATO SI', MI' SIGNORE.` · `BROTHER SUN, SISTER MOON.` · `SISTER WATER, MOTHER EARTH.` · `SISTER BODILY DEATH.` · then, large: `ALL CREATION PRAISING.`

segments.voice: Step outside if you can, or open a window. Listen for one sound at a time, a breath each: wind, water, a bird, a voice, your own feet on the earth. If you know the Canticle, pray it whole out there; otherwise, simply call each sound brother or sister as it comes.
The Canticle. Francis's song where sun, moon, wind, water, fire, earth and even death are family, and all of them praising.
Hold onto this: all creation praising, even the sister nobody invites to dinner. Until next time.

notes: The Canticle is paraphrased (Matthew Arnold's 1865 translation is public domain but not on the validator's list, and the spoken text follows the Italian, not his wording). Confirm the order and epithets: the opening to the Most High; Brother Sun who is the day and bears God's likeness; Sister Moon and stars; Brother Wind, air, cloud and all weather; Sister Water useful, humble, precious, chaste ('pure' in the script); Brother Fire beautiful, jocund, robust, strong ('cheerful and strong'); Sister our Mother Earth who sustains and governs us, with fruits, colored flowers and herbs; those who forgive and endure; Sister Bodily Death; the closing praise with great humility. The script leaves out the lines on mortal sin and the second death for length.
'Tradition says' Francis added the forgiveness and death verses later, the death verse near the end of his life; no dates given.
For parents: the lesson and Sofia's chat name death directly (a grandmother planning her funeral songs), gently and without fear.
